text.p: A short-lived rash of dollar-buying after news Russia planned to chop three zeroes off its currency ended on Monday even before full details of the rouble reform were published, returning the rouble to its opening levels, dealers said.
rouble/dollar Aug 4 Aug 1
midday morning close
tomorrow settlement 5,800-01 5,799-00 5,800-01
overnight credits (%) 9-14 11-16 10-14
Dealers said the dollar buying was a short emotional outburst and they did not expect the coming reform to seriously affect the currency market.

President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday the redenomination would be one for 1,000 from January 1, 1998, and reassured Russians there would be a lengthy exchange period, and people would not be forced to swap their old notes in a short period.
"The first announcement, of course, overwhelmed many people and they took the first and the most simple decision -- to buy dollars," one trader said.
"But as soon as rumours started circulating that the reform would start from January, a very natural reverse move took place."
Traders said the news was now well understood by the market and no new outbursts were expected.
"Second thoughts on the reform are unlikely. There will be no new influence on the market from today's news," said another trader.
The central bank, traders said, had a strong grip on the forex market and would do its best to avoid any sharp fluctuations.

Dealers said the central bank was capable of smoothing down rouble fluctuations with its heavy hard currency reserves. The central bank said its net international reserves had doubled in the last month to 60.9 trillion roubles on July 1. Gross reserves were $23.8 billion.
They said that after midday some traditional factors, such as compulsory reserve payments by banks and clients' orders were likely to have more influence on the rouble rate than the reform.
"Overnight rouble credit interest rates, which started rising on Friday, are still rising. Maybe this is linked with banks' reserve payments and clients' operations," one dealer said.
The fact that the reform will start in January and will last for a long period means it can be assumed the rouble will not suffer a major nosedive, traders said.

A dealer said the rouble should in theory become stronger as a result of the redenomination, but there was a possiblity of panic on the cash market as ordinary people might not listen to the details but rush into dollars as a safe haven.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
